note: Ground truth + grading rubric. DO NOT feed to the SLM. Score each episode on the rubric below.

VFIB-STEMI-001.primaryEtiology: Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (anterior/LAD) precipitating ventricular fibrillation arrest
VFIB-STEMI-001.mechanism: Ischemia-driven electrical instability (R-on-T) degenerating to VF
contributing: Known CAD with prior LAD stent
Markedly elevated troponin T / CK-MB
Anterior ST elevation pre-arrest
Metabolic acidosis/elevated lactate from arrest
distractors: Do NOT attribute to hyperkalemia (K normal 4.1)
Do NOT call it a benign arrhythmia

TORSADES-LQT-002.primaryEtiology: Acquired long-QT syndrome causing Torsades de pointes
TORSADES-LQT-002.mechanism: QT prolongation from combined QT-prolonging drugs (sotalol + azithromycin + ondansetron) and hypokalemia/hypomagnesemia
contributing: QTc 618 ms on baseline ECG
Hypokalemia 2.9 and hypomagnesemia 1.2
GI losses from gastroenteritis
Multiple QT-prolonging medications
mustRecommend: Stop all QT-prolonging drugs (sotalol, azithromycin, ondansetron)
Consider overdrive pacing/isoproterenol; defibrillate if sustained/unstable
distractors: Not ischemic monomorphic VT (troponin only mildly up, rate-related)
Not primarily electrolyte-independent

VT-ISCHEMIC-003.primaryEtiology: Scar-related reentrant monomorphic VT in ischemic cardiomyopathy
VT-ISCHEMIC-003.mechanism: Reentry around myocardial scar from prior infarct; not acute ischemia
contributing: Ischemic cardiomyopathy LVEF 25% with prior infarct
AV dissociation/fusion beats confirming VT
Only mild demand troponin (no STEMI)
Electrolytes normal
mustRecommend: Synchronized cardioversion if it becomes unstable
distractors: Not SVT with aberrancy (AV dissociation + fusion beats present)
Not acute STEMI (troponin only mildly elevated, no ST elevation)
Not Torsades (monomorphic, normal QT/K/Mg)

AFIB-RVR-SEPSIS-004.display: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
AFIB-RVR-SEPSIS-004.primaryEtiology: New-onset atrial fibrillation with RVR triggered by sepsis (urosepsis)
AFIB-RVR-SEPSIS-004.mechanism: Systemic inflammation, catecholamine surge, fever and volume shifts precipitating AFib in a susceptible atrium
contributing: Fever 38.9, WBC 18.4, procalcitonin 6.2, lactate 3.1 (sepsis)
No prior AFib
On vasopressor for septic shock
mustIdentify: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
mustRecommend: Treat the underlying sepsis (antibiotics, source control, fluids)
Rate control cautiously given hypotension (avoid worsening shock)
distractors: Not primary cardiac arrhythmia to cardiovert first-line (treat sepsis)
Not thyrotoxicosis (TSH normal)
Not ACS (troponin only mildly up)

CHB-HYPERK-005.primaryEtiology: Severe hyperkalemia (K 7.4) from missed dialysis causing high-grade AV block and bradycardia
CHB-HYPERK-005.mechanism: Hyperkalemia depresses conduction — peaked T waves, QRS widening, AV block, bradycardia
contributing: K 7.4 with peaked T waves and wide QRS
Missed hemodialysis, ESRD, Cr 9.8
Potassium-sparing meds (lisinopril, spironolactone)
Metabolic acidosis
mustIdentify: Hyperkalemic ECG changes (peaked T, wide QRS)
mustRecommend: Hold lisinopril/spironolactone; transcutaneous pacing if needed
distractors: Do NOT treat as isolated conduction disease needing only a pacemaker — reverse hyperkalemia first
Not primarily ischemic

BRADY-DIGTOX-006.primaryEtiology: Digoxin toxicity (level 3.8) precipitated by acute kidney injury
BRADY-DIGTOX-006.mechanism: Digoxin accumulation with AKI causing increased vagal tone/AV block — regularized AF, junctional bradycardia, GI and visual symptoms
contributing: Digoxin level 3.8 (toxic)
AKI (Cr 2.1) reducing clearance
Hyperkalemia 5.6 (marker of significant toxicity)
Classic symptoms: nausea/vomiting, yellow-green vision
Regularized AFib + scooped ST (dig effect)
mustRecommend: Digoxin-specific antibody fragments (DigiFab) for significant toxicity/hyperkalemia
Avoid calcium for the hyperkalemia if possible; treat toxicity
distractors: Do NOT treat hyperkalemia 5.6 with IV calcium reflexively (relative caution in dig toxicity)
Not primary sinus node disease

SVT-PSVT-007.mechanism: AV-nodal reentry; benign in a young healthy patient, caffeine as trigger
contributing: Young healthy patient with recurrent self-terminating episodes
Caffeine trigger
Normal electrolytes, thyroid, troponin
mustRecommend: Rate-limiting agents / EP referral for recurrence
distractors: Not VT (narrow QRS)
Not sinus tachycardia from sepsis/hypovolemia (abrupt onset, no fever, normal labs)
Not thyrotoxicosis (TSH normal)

NSVT-ECTOPY-008.display: Frequent PVCs with non-sustained VT run
NSVT-ECTOPY-008.mechanism: Hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia (thiazide-induced, post-op) increasing ventricular irritability
contributing: K 3.1 and Mg 1.5 (thiazide + post-op)
Rising PVC burden with a short NSVT run
Hemodynamically stable, asymptomatic
mustRecommend: Reassess PVC burden after correction; avoid unnecessary antiarrhythmics
distractors: Not sustained VT requiring cardioversion (non-sustained, stable)
Not acute ischemia (troponin minimal, no ST changes)

WCT-DIFF-009.primaryEtiology: Scar-related reentrant monomorphic ventricular tachycardia in ischemic cardiomyopathy
WCT-DIFF-009.mechanism: Reentry around anterior myocardial scar from prior MI; hemodynamic stability does NOT exclude VT — 46-71% of VT episodes are hemodynamically tolerated
contributing: Prior anterior MI with LVEF 35% (substrate for reentry)
AV dissociation with capture beats (pathognomonic for VT)
Monophasic R in V1 (not typical rSR' of RBBB aberrancy)
QS pattern in V6 (favors VT over SVT with aberrancy)
Left axis deviation with RBBB-type morphology
Precordial concordance (negative V1-V4)
Normal electrolytes (argues against metabolic cause)
mustIdentify: AV dissociation and capture beats as pathognomonic VT features
Hemodynamic stability does NOT exclude VT
mustRecommend: Do NOT administer verapamil or diltiazem
distractors: Do NOT diagnose as SVT with aberrancy based on hemodynamic stability
Do NOT administer verapamil or diltiazem (can cause VF/asystole in VT — 44-59% serious adverse effects)
Not sinus tachycardia (regular WCT with AV dissociation)
Not thyrotoxicosis (TSH normal)

WPW-AFIB-010.primaryEtiology: Pre-excited atrial fibrillation via accessory pathway (Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome)
WPW-AFIB-010.mechanism: Atrial fibrillation with antegrade conduction over an accessory pathway, bypassing the AV node's rate-limiting function; beat-to-beat QRS variation reflects varying degrees of fusion between AP and AV nodal conduction; shortest R-R ~200 ms indicates high-risk pathway (ERP <250 ms)
contributing: Irregularly irregular wide-complex tachycardia with beat-to-beat QRS width variation (120-200 ms)
Delta waves visible in wider beats
Shortest R-R interval ~200 ms (high-risk accessory pathway)
Young healthy male with prior episodes of rapid heart rate
QRS polarity does not vary along baseline (distinguishes from polymorphic VT)
Normal electrolytes and troponin
mustIdentify: Beat-to-beat QRS variation as hallmark feature
mustRecommend: If stable: IV procainamide or ibutilide
Do NOT administer ANY AV nodal blocking agent
Catheter ablation of accessory pathway (definitive therapy)
distractors: Do NOT administer verapamil or diltiazem (Class III: Harm — can accelerate AP conduction → VF)
Do NOT administer IV amiodarone (AV nodal block precedes AP effect → can worsen)
Do NOT administer beta-blockers (AV nodal block removes concealed conduction protection)
Do NOT administer digoxin (directly shortens AP refractory period)
Do NOT administer adenosine (potent AV nodal block → can trigger VF)
Not polymorphic VT (QRS polarity stable; irregular rhythm with delta waves)
Not standard AF with aberrancy (beat-to-beat QRS variation with delta waves is pathognomonic for preexcitation)

FLUTTER-IC-011.primaryEtiology: Flecainide-induced 1:1 atrial flutter with use-dependent QRS widening
FLUTTER-IC-011.mechanism: Flecainide organized AF into atrial flutter and slowed the atrial rate from ~300 to ~200 bpm; without an AV nodal blocker, the AV node conducts every flutter wave 1:1; use-dependent sodium channel blockade widens QRS at fast rates (180 ms vs baseline 88 ms), mimicking VT
contributing: Flecainide 100 mg BID without AV nodal blocker co-prescription (prescribing error)
Regular WCT at 200 bpm (1:1 flutter conduction)
QRS 180 ms (widened from baseline 88 ms — use-dependent Na-channel block)
Flutter waves faintly visible in V1
Sharp initial QRS deflection (His-Purkinje engagement — argues against VT)
No structural heart disease (normal echo)
Normal electrolytes
mustIdentify: Use-dependent QRS widening from sodium channel blockade
Missing AV nodal blocker as the prescribing error
mustRecommend: IV beta-blocker (esmolol) to slow AV conduction if stable
IV sodium bicarbonate for QRS widening (sodium channel blocker toxicity)
Discontinue flecainide or add mandatory AV nodal blocker
Do NOT add additional antiarrhythmic drugs (proarrhythmic escalation)
distractors: Do NOT diagnose as VT (sharp initial QRS deflection, no structural heart disease, flutter waves visible)
Do NOT administer lidocaine or procainamide (additional sodium channel blockade worsens toxicity)
Do NOT administer amiodarone (additional sodium channel blockade + proarrhythmic)
Not primary VT (no structural heart disease, drug-induced mechanism)

PERI-STEMI-012.primaryEtiology: Acute viral pericarditis (post-viral, likely myopericarditis given mild troponin elevation)
PERI-STEMI-012.mechanism: Viral-mediated pericardial inflammation causing diffuse subepicardial injury; ST elevation reflects epicardial inflammation rather than coronary occlusion
contributing: Diffuse concave ST elevation not conforming to coronary territory
PR-segment depression in limb and precordial leads (PPV 96.7% for pericarditis vs STEMI)
Absence of reciprocal ST depression (OR 31 for pericarditis vs STEMI)
ST/T ratio 0.28 in V6 (≥0.25 supports pericarditis)
Sharp pleuritic positional chest pain with trapezius radiation
Pericardial friction rub on exam
Recent URI (viral prodrome)
Elevated CRP 4.8 mg/dL and ESR 38 (inflammatory markers)
Normal BNP (argues against heart failure)
Young male with no cardiac risk factors
mustIdentify: PR-segment depression as key distinguishing feature
mustRecommend: NSAIDs (ibuprofen 600 mg TID) + colchicine 0.5 mg BID
Echocardiogram to assess for pericardial effusion and LV function
Serial troponin to assess for myopericarditis component
distractors: Do NOT activate STEMI protocol (diffuse non-territorial ST elevation, PR depression, no reciprocal changes)
Do NOT administer antiplatelet loading or anticoagulation for ACS
Not STEMI (no territorial distribution, no reciprocal changes, PR depression present)
Troponin 0.03 is consistent with myopericarditis, not ACS (CRP/troponin ratio >>100)

BRASH-013.primaryEtiology: BRASH syndrome (Bradycardia, Renal failure, AV blockade, Shock, Hyperkalemia) — synergistic cycle of AV-nodal blockade (atenolol) + hyperkalemia + AKI
BRASH-013.mechanism: Hypovolemia from poor oral intake → prerenal AKI → impaired clearance of both potassium and atenolol → synergistic bradycardia disproportionate to either insult alone → decreased cardiac output → worsening renal perfusion → further AKI → vicious cycle; ECG changes are characteristically milder than expected for K+ level because the AV-nodal blocker is the primary bradycardia driver
contributing: Atenolol (AV-nodal blocker) + lisinopril (K+-sparing) + CKD (impaired clearance)
K+ 6.4 mmol/L (moderate — would not typically cause HR 32 alone)
Creatinine 3.2 mg/dL (baseline 1.4 — acute kidney injury)
HR 32 bpm with shock (MAP 53) — disproportionate to K+ level
ECG changes mild relative to K+ (only mild peaked T waves, QRS 108 ms — not classic hyperkalemic progression)
Atropine failure x2 (characteristic of BRASH — atropine ineffective in 59.5% of cases)
3 days poor oral intake (hypovolemia as precipitant)
Elevated lactate 4.2 (tissue hypoperfusion from shock)
mustIdentify: BRASH syndrome (synergistic mechanism, not isolated hyperkalemia or isolated beta-blocker effect)
Disproportionate bradycardia/shock relative to K+ level
AKI from prerenal azotemia as the precipitant
mustRecommend: Aggressive IV fluid resuscitation (address hypovolemia — the precipitant)
Epinephrine infusion if refractory to above (preferred chronotrope/vasopressor when atropine fails)
Transcutaneous pacing as bridge if needed
distractors: Do NOT treat as isolated hyperkalemia (K+ 6.4 alone would not cause HR 32 with shock)
Do NOT treat as isolated beta-blocker toxicity (K+ is a critical co-factor)
Do NOT rely on atropine alone (characteristically ineffective in BRASH)
Do NOT attribute to primary conduction system disease requiring permanent pacemaker (reversible once cycle is broken — 0% of BRASH patients need permanent pacing)
Not sepsis (afebrile, no infectious source)

AMIO-DDI-014.primaryEtiology: Triple amiodarone drug interaction cascade: (1) CYP2C9 inhibition → warfarin accumulation (INR 5.8), (2) P-glycoprotein inhibition → digoxin accumulation (level 2.4 ng/mL), (3) CYP3A4 inhibition → simvastatin accumulation (CK 1200 U/L)
AMIO-DDI-014.mechanism: Amiodarone and its metabolite desethylamiodarone inhibit multiple drug-metabolizing enzymes and transporters simultaneously; all three clinical manifestations (supratherapeutic INR, digoxin toxicity, statin myopathy) share a single common cause — the newly initiated amiodarone
contributing: INR rose from 2.4 to 5.8 within 4 days of amiodarone (CYP2C9 inhibition doubles warfarin effect)
Digoxin level rose from 1.0 to 2.4 ng/mL (P-gp inhibition increases digoxin ~70-100%)
CK 1200 U/L with muscle aches (CYP3A4 inhibition increases simvastatin AUC ~75%)
Scooped ST segments (digoxin effect on ECG)
QTc 510 ms (amiodarone-induced QT prolongation)
Bradycardia HR 48 (synergistic effect of amiodarone + digoxin + carvedilol on AV node)
No dose adjustments made for any interacting drug when amiodarone was started
mustIdentify: Amiodarone as the single common cause of all three drug interactions
All three manifestations are drug interactions, not independent events
mustRecommend: Reduce warfarin dose by 33-50%; hold warfarin until INR <3; consider vitamin K if bleeding
Reduce digoxin dose by 50% or hold; recheck level in 1 week
Switch simvastatin to ≤20 mg daily OR change to pravastatin/rosuvastatin (not CYP3A4 substrates)
Monitor INR frequently (q2-3 days) until stable
Monitor CK serially; hold statin if CK >10x ULN or symptoms worsen
Adjust amiodarone to maintenance dose; monitor for additional toxicities (thyroid, pulmonary, hepatic)
distractors: Do NOT attribute INR elevation to dietary change or warfarin dose error alone
Do NOT attribute digoxin toxicity to renal impairment alone (Cr 1.3 is normal)
Do NOT attribute CK elevation to rhabdomyolysis from other cause without considering statin interaction
Do NOT continue all three interacting drugs at current doses
Not thyroid dysfunction (TSH normal — though amiodarone can cause thyroid disease, onset is typically weeks to months)
